The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

Manchester United have been urged to make a major effort to sign Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall during the January transfer window as they look to address their defensive problems under Mauricio Pochettino.

The Red Devils are expected to explore opportunities to strengthen their backline in the coming months, and the England international has emerged as a particularly attractive option.

According to a report via TEAMtalk, former Manchester United midfielder Quinton Fortune believes his old club should prioritise a move for the 22-year-old after his impressive performances for England against Spain.

“Lewis Hall is the best! Lewis Hall is the best left-back in the Premier League, and I cannot even let you finish the sentence. I watched him the other night against Spain.

“Come on. First of all, I’m putting it out there, Manchester United have to go and get him. There’s no doubt. That guy is unbelievable.

“Against Spain the other night, I knew he was good, but I didn’t know he was that good.

“My goodness. Go and get him. Whatever it takes. I don’t care. Go and get him. I can’t keep that image out of my head. I watched him the other night, I was almost crying watching him against Spain like, ‘Why can’t we just go and get this guy? Just go and get him.’

“I would have done the deal after the game. I would have been in the changing room after the game like, ‘Just call him, please. Let’s do the deal right here.’ Oh goodness, what a player.”

Fortune was particularly impressed by the Newcastle defender’s display against the European champions and believes he has the qualities needed to improve United’s options at left-back.

The former Chelsea academy graduate has developed into one of the most promising young defenders in English football. His technical ability, attacking instincts and defensive awareness could make him an excellent addition to the Manchester United squad.

United have struggled considerably at the back this season, conceding 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions. Strengthening the defensive department will therefore be an important task for Pochettino as he attempts to turn the club’s fortunes around.

However, convincing Newcastle to part ways with their prized asset will not be straightforward. The Magpies have already demonstrated their determination to retain the defender by handing him a new long-term contract in September.

Hall remains an important component of their plans, and they are unlikely to entertain his departure midway through the campaign.

Manchester United could certainly benefit from investing in a specialist left-back, but they may need to consider alternative targets if Newcastle refuse to negotiate.

Nevertheless, Hall would be an exciting long-term addition at Old Trafford.

#1280. Glucose-powered implant brings devices for treating diabetes a step closer

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. Junta Imai is in the Department of Diabetes, Metabolism and Endocrinology, Tohoku University Graduate School of Medicine, Aoba-ku, Sendai, Miyagi 980-8575, Japan.

Hundreds of millions of people around the world are affected by diabetes mellitus1. It develops when the activity of insulin, a glucose-lowering hormone secreted by pancreatic β-cells, becomes insufficient to maintain healthy glucose levels in the blood. The condition can be managed with oral medication or by injecting insulin and other metabolic hormones, but the constant need for people with diabetes to manage their lifestyle and blood-glucose levels can impair their quality of life. Therapeutic approaches that monitor and control blood glucose automatically are therefore highly desirable. Writing in Nature, Xiu et al.2 report proof of principle of a bioelectronic device called NeuroAxis that does exactly that in rat models of diabetes.

#1279. MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

And that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

That’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up big-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

It was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

The South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

An initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

Motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Said, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

#1277. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

It had escaped my attention that Arsenal defender Gabriel is facing his former club tonight. At £27m, signed in 2020, he has to go down as one of Arteta’s best signings, and one of the best value signings any Premier League club has made this decade.

It’s very difficult. You come across very special people in life and Ken was certainly one of them. He’s an absolute legend of this football club. I think he’s the soul of this football club and someone that has given his life to this club.

Lille’s manager is Davide Ancelotti, the son of Carlo, and you would assume he has picked up a few tips and tricks from his dad about success in this competition. Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

“LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1276. Rangers boss Derek McInnes salutes never-say-die attitude of his side and was always confident of the winning goal arriving

Published: 18:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:22 EST, 21 November 2026

Rangers manager Derek McInnes praised his side for having the mentality to grind out last-gasp winners and hailed their late victory over Motherwell as a ‘top-class performance’.

McInnes admits he would have liked a more comfortable evening from a match which saw his side fire 29 shots with 11 on target, but he was happy with the level of chance creation and delighted to see Ryan Naderi serve up yet another crucial goal with a deflected effort that made the difference two minutes from time.

Rangers had opened brightly with a Manny Fernandez goal on eight minutes, but looked like sliding to a third straight league draw away from home after Jake Girdwood-Reich had levelled for the home side in the first half.

‘I thought it was a very good, strong performance. I’ve just been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot,’ said McInnes, whose men are four points behind Celtic with a game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday.

‘I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week. It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance.

‘Away from home in the Premiership, you’re never going to dominate a whole game. There were little spells Motherwell had on transitions, but our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time

Ryan naderi scored the dramatic late winner for Rangers as they closed the gap on Celtic

‘Equally, on the sidelines, I felt a goal was coming. It’s OK me feeling that, but I think the players feel it too and it’s important they do. It would have been such a body blow if we hadn’t found a winning goal, given the stats and the performance.

‘It’s a tough away game and it’s the first time we’ve won here in three years, so that illustrates that.

‘When we pick the bones out of it, there will be a lot of what we ask for in that game.

‘It’s good that we’ve got that in us, a last minute goal, because we know how important they are in a campaign. I’ve never found mental strength an issue for my side.

‘On this fantastic run, we’ve been very strong. We were by far the better team. We dominated the chances and a lot of what I was hoping for was there.

‘It was just that execution. We’ve had this story before, but, as long as we keep winning, I’m all right with that.

‘I’m getting asked about not putting teams to bed. That’s another away game with two goals. It’s four in a row now. In our last two home games, we’ve scored four and three, so scoring goals isn’t really causing a problem, even if people are looking for a negative.

‘I think that performance was an improvement from where we’ve been in recent weeks.’

McInnes also reserved special praise for matchwinner Naderi.

‘Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,’ said the manager. ‘Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in.

‘His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a big horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure, but he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most important position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball.

Manny Fernandez opened the scoring for the Ibrox men in the 2-1 victory

‘He led the line brilliantly. It was a proper No 9 performance.

Naderi admits he is delighted to be scoring messy goals that are making a real impact on his side’s challenge for the title.

‘I like those games. Of course we would like to win 3-0, but, when you win in the last minute, that's something special,’ said the Czech internationalist.

‘I can't score nice goals, only ugly ones.’

Motherwell head coach Alfred Johansson said: ‘It is obviously tough to concede that goal at the very end. We had a feeling we could finish the game with a draw.

‘I think Rangers were better than us. They had a good start to the game and it was tough for us conceding a goal from a set-piece when we are not aggressive enough.

‘At the end, we lost the energy. Rangers were turning up the heat in the last 15, 20 minutes. We were fighting and surviving and then they scored.

‘Alex Paulsen played fantastic in goal. He has been making a lot of saves for us this season and, at the end, it is tough for him to concede a goal like that.’

Tottenham Hotspur are keeping Samu Aghehowa on their radar as Roberto De Zerbi continues to explore options to strengthen his attacking department ahead of the January transfer window.

The Porto striker has attracted interest from the North London club, with the Spanish forward emerging as another option as Spurs look to add more firepower to their squad.

Aghehowa has developed into a prolific goalscorer in Portuguese football, registering 49 goals in 85 appearances across all competitions for the club. His impressive return includes 25 goals during his debut campaign and another 19 strikes last season.

#1274. Intra-stellar: a star inside a giant star

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Jason Nordhaus is at the Center for Computational Relativity and Gravitation and the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, Rochester Institute of Technology, Rochester, New York 14623, USA.

Towards the end of their lives, stars experience a drastic change in their structure as they swell and enter what is known as their giant phase. Because most stars are thought to host orbiting companions (such as planets, other stars or black holes), interesting interactions can happen as the giant host expands. The most striking of these occur when a companion star is engulfed by a giant: astronomers refer to this as the common-envelope phase1. Despite theoretical expectations that common envelopes should be widespread in stellar evolution, they have been extraordinarily difficult to observe. Writing in Nature, however, Karambelkar et al.2 report the first direct detection of a star inside a giant star.

#1272. Frustrated Cole Palmer shares frosty exchange with Joao Pedro after upsetting Chelsea staff member before walking off down the tunnel after 4-1 drubbing by Leeds

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

#1271. Ex-Aston Villa Striker Donyell Malen Drawing Interest Following Rich Roma

Donyell Malen is drawing Premier League interest, GIVEMESPORT understands, after a sensational season so far at Roma.

The former Aston Villa forward scored four times in Saturday’s 5-1 win at Parma to take his tally to 26 Serie A goals in 2026. That equals a Roma record for league goals in a calendar year, set by Pedro Manfredini in 1960 – and is more league goals than Harry Kane or Kylian Mbappe have managed in that time.

A January move would be difficult, though. Roma, two points behind leaders Lazio, do not want to sell Serie A’s top scorer, who is under contract until 2030. Roma could even offer Malen improved terms to stave off any interest.

Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his Manchester United career against Liverpool

Manchester United and Tottenham have both looked at the 27-year-old in the past, including during his time at Borussia Dortmund. Newcastle United are also believed to have discussed the striker over the summer.

Finding a new striker is a high priority in United's January transfer plans. Benjamin Sesko is out until the new year with a shin injury, Joshua Zirkzee could leave in January, and Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday that left them second from bottom.

They got a close look at Malen earlier this month, too, when he scored a penalty in Roma’s 3-2 Champions League defeat at Old Trafford.

But it is believed United are looking for more of an old-fashioned No 9. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is one name to have been considered, but he is expected to sign a new deal at Elland Road.

Malen’s time at Villa did not go to plan. He scored 10 goals in 46 appearances after joining from Dortmund in January 2025, and left on loan for Roma a year later. The Giallorossi made the move permanent at the end of last season.

The key has been his position. Only around half of Malen’s league minutes at Villa came as a central striker. Under Gian Piero Gasperini, he has been utilised through the middle.

Malen told Corriere dello Sport last month that leaving Villa was his decision.

“I wanted to play and be part of a team where I could take the field every weekend and play an important role,” he said. “At that stage, I didn’t feel important, so I think I made the best choice.”

Gasperini, speaking at the Festival dello Sport in Trento earlier this season, said: “There were a few names on the table, suddenly we heard that Aston Villa were selling Malen due to tactical issues.

“He wanted to be a centre-forward, and I always thought that’s where he was stronger too, as he’s deadly near the penalty area. Admittedly, I didn’t expect his numbers to be so astonishing. I told him Gonzalo Higuain scored 36 Serie A goals in a season, but I’d be happy if he got to 30.”

Malen needs one more goal to make Manfredini’s record his own. Roma host Monza on Sunday, after a Champions League trip to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.

PSG have also been linked with a move for the Roma forward, but GMS understands should he leave Roma, a switch back to the Premier League would be of appeal in the long-run, but he is happy at Roma currently.

#1269. 16 Best Footballers to Never Win a League Title [Ranked]

Football is often about personal glory for players in the modern day, with very few ever showing immense levels of loyalty. However, there have been a handful of players over the years who have either stayed loyal or never been at a club good enough to win a league title.

After years of failure at Tottenham Hotspur, England captain Harry Kane moved to Bayern Munich in pursuit of his first league crown. In his debut season, 2023/2024, he saw his team pipped by Bayer Leverkusen for the Bundesliga title but finally ended his career drought by winning the league in Germany a year later. He has since won that title again in 2026.

Marco Reus was also originally on the list, but after years of near misses with Borussia Dortmund, he claimed an MLS league title in America in 2024 with New York Red Bulls.

These 16 players, however, never quite got their hands on that elusive top-flight league title. Instead, they have been remembered as the best players who, sometimes narrowly, missed out.

While Kane left Tottenham Hotspur to put an end to his title-hunting misery, Son Heung-min remained in north London and finally won the first major honour of his career as Spurs lifted the 2025 Europa League. Before that, the South Korean had been a runner-up in the Champions League and League Cup, and also finished second in the 2016/17 Premier League season (Spurs' highest league finish since the 1962–63 season) but has not been able to get his hands on a league trophy.

That doesn't change the fact that Son is a brilliant footballer, as proven by the fact that he has 127 Premier League goals, the 16th highest in competition history. Now in his 30s, and playing in MLS for Los Angeles FC, it will be interesting to see if he can win a league title before he hangs up his boots.

Kickstarting the list, Daniele De Rossi was one of the most consistent players throughout his career. The Italian solidified Roma's midfield every single season, acting as a transitional player between defence and attack. A player as important that often wins a title, but not De Rossi.

He came close on three separate occasions, yet Roma never got it over the line. In the 2016/2017 season, they finished on 87 points - a remarkable feat - yet still four points adrift of Italian champions Juventus. It epitomised De Rossi's luck in Italy, as, despite all his quality, he never won the most wanted trophy in the country - the Serie A.

Bruno Fernandes is one of Manchester United's greatest ever footballers. He proved that in the 2025/26 season, breaking the Premier League assist record (21) and being named as the competition's Player of the Year. Unfortunately, though, he has played for the club in an era of underperformance.

Under Sir Alex Ferguson, Fernandes would have won many titles, but the midfielder has not enjoyed success on that level during his time at Old Trafford. Before coming to England, he lifted two cups with Sporting CP, but never won the Portuguese league, and his time in Italy's top flight with Udinese and Sampdoria also failed to yield an elusive league title.

Now best known for his on-screen personality, Jamie Carragher became a one-club man by spending all 17 of his senior seasons with Premier League outfit Liverpool, and although he was part of the iconic Reds side that won the Champions League in 2005, he was unable to lift Premier League gold in that period.

GIVEMESPORT looks at players who went from being footballing enemies to wholehearted friends.

His side’s best efforts came in 2001/02 and 2008/09 when the Merseysiders concluded the season in 2nd place, finishing with 80 and 96 points, respectively. And while he enjoys bickering with his former foe Gary Neville on television, one thing he cannot compete with the latter’s trophy collection, particularly in terms of league titles.

Out of the five English clubs Robbie Fowler plied his trade for, 80% (four) of them have won a league title since 1990 – Leeds, Liverpool, Blackburn Rovers and Manchester City. The Englishman, however, had moved on by then. A scorer of 163 Premier League goals, the marksman enjoyed his brightest spell on Merseyside and won plenty of trophies there.

That included four major honours – including a cup treble in 2001 – but he never managed to get his hands on a league title, with his highest finish being 3rd. Upon his departure, he failed to recapture his former Anfield form, which earned him the moniker of ‘God’, and that in itself made becoming a champion all the more difficult.

There have been many wonderful British football players in history - here are the 15 best including Wayne Rooney and Gareth Bale.

A fleet-footed winger who will forever be enshrined in football mythology, Jay-Jay Okocha never reached the promised land of club football – becoming a league winner, that is. His glitz and glamour aside, the Nigerian played for some top clubs in his heyday, such as Paris Saint-Germain and Fenerbahce.

While in the French capital, Okocha only managed a second-place finish in 1999/00 and his two-season spell at Fenerbahce beforehand was just as disheartening. They finished third in 1996/97 and second in the following campaign. There was no doubting the former Bolton gem’s ungodly talent, but perhaps it was a case of being in the right place at the wrong time.

When you think of hit-and-miss strikers, you probably think of Fernando Torres. On his day, he was one of the best players in the world - as showcased at Atletico Madrid and Liverpool. Yet he also struggled, including his disastrous spell at Chelsea. He went his entire career without winning a league title, despite coming close so many times.

In the 2008/2009 season, Liverpool finished on 86 points, four points adrift of champions Manchester United. Torres scored the fourth most goals in the league that season (14), but even the Spaniard’s prolific nature in front of goal couldn't help the Reds over the line.

Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink may not be revered as a world-class superstar but his goals speak for themselves, stationed as the top tier’s 16th-highest goalscorer – above the likes of Premier League greats Cristiano Ronaldo and Ian Wright. The gifted Dutchman was a two-time Golden Boot winner but still couldn’t bring home what every kid dreams of.

Hasselbaink, now a Technical Coach for the Three Lions, was a runner-up in the Premier League and FA Cup with Chelsea. His top-class performances for the Blues are largely forgotten about thanks to the fact that they were a less sturdy force in those days. Even with Leeds, the closest he came to becoming a league champion was in 1998/99 when they finished fourth.

Gary Lineker always jokes with Alan Shearer when on TV about trophies during their respective careers. Shearer never won the FA Cup, but Lineker somehow never won a league title during his playing days. Lineker left boyhood club Leicester for Everton in pursuit of ample silverware, but he fell narrowly short.

In the 1985/1986 season, they finished second on 86 points, two points behind bitter rivals Liverpool. Even when he moved to Spanish juggernauts Barcelona - and eventually Tottenham - he was never able to get his hands on a league title, despite being one of the best goalscorers of all time.

Antoine Griezmann has been one of the most entertaining players to watch during the modern-day generation, gliding past defenders effortlessly. Yet, he has never won a top-flight league title, but did lift the Segunda Division with Real Sociedad in 2009/10. Incredibly, Griezmann has joined Atletico Madrid twice as reigning champions, but he has never won La Liga with them.

The European Championships have seen the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Zinedine Zidane and Xavi, but who's the best of the lot?

He came close while at Barcelona on two occasions during his brief spell on the Mediterranean coast, with 73 points and 82 points on two occasions, but it was never enough to beat their rivals. As his move to Orlando City has been confirmed, he will never win a La Liga title but will hope to lift an MLS title in America. Upon his Atletico exit, he emotionally admitted regret about leaving the club for Barcelona, which cost him a title in the Spanish capital:

“Please forgive me. I was young and I made a mistake to join Barcelona. I did not understand the love I had here. I recognised my mistake, and did everything to come back and enjoy here. I didn’t win La Liga or the Champions League, but your love is what matters.”

#1268. Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

This feels a big moment for Carrick and United’s players to answer some of their critics. They have been getting battered from all sides in the last couple of days. Nicky Butt suggested on his podcast that Carrick told him before he got the United job that management “not for me” and “my head’s all over the shop” and that United was the only job he would take. At the very least, those comments are unhelpful and they are thought to have been dimly received internally.

Jamie Carragher offered a lacerating analysis of United’s performance against Spurs on Saturday on Sky Sports on Monday night and suggested things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved if there is not marked improvement. Steven Gerrard questioned why United opted to invest £50m of their summer budget in Andrey Santos, an unused substitute in the last three league games, insisted the back four was not good enough and questioned the work ethic.

And it was interesting to see Carrick alongside his mate Wayne Rooney just now pitchside. Rooney told the Stick to United podcast that captain Bruno Fernandes looks “fed up” and ready to explode at any moment.

It would have been pretty unthinkable for Carrick not to run with a three-man midfield here, not just because of the wide open spaces opponents have exploited this season but when you look at the back line United are fielding. Dalot at left back, two youngsters in Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven and a horribly out of form Lisandro Maríinez.

Nor has Senne Lammens looked convincing this term. Matheus Cunha has been dropped – not before time – and I expect to see Fernandes playing off the right. There’s going to a big onus on Rashford on the left. I’m not sure if he is fully fit but he’s going to be important.

It’s fantastic. It’s where we want to be, these games, these competitions. It’s as tough a place as you can come to. They’ve got a really good history in this competition and it’s where we want to come to challenge and test ourselves. We have put ourselves in this position, got a good start at home and now this is our first away game.

We want a reaction, of course. A positive reaction [to Saturday’s poor performance]. It hasn’t gone how we wanted, how we expected so far but it’s been fine margins in some of those games. It can go both ways but the reality is where we are at now.

It’s a fresh night and we’ve got to adapt, we’ve got to adjust in a positive way.

We want a little more control in the game [with three central midfielders]. At times we have been too open. We wanted to make a difference in that way. We’ve made other changes, certain spaces, certain positions.

To be honest it’s not really a big change of shape, personnel maybe but a lot of it is similar. We want more control, a little bit without the ball and a lot more with it. We’re happy with the way we set up.

Look at the last three goals we’ve conceded. They’re a mixed bag, simple goals you can something about. We need to defend better as a whole team .

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

Newcastle United and Chelsea are reportedly preparing to battle for the signature of highly-rated Hearts youngster Jaedon Donkor ahead of the January transfer window.

The 17-year-old winger has attracted considerable attention following his impressive performances in Scotland, with several clubs monitoring his development ahead of a potential move.

According to a Football Insider report, both Premier League clubs are exploring the possibility of bringing Donkor to England in January.

The teenager is approaching the final months of his contract at Tynecastle, with Hearts keen to secure his long-term future and fend off interest from potential suitors.

Donkor’s contract situation has put several clubs on alert, with Newcastle and Chelsea among those keen to exploit the uncertainty surrounding his future.

The London-born attacker previously spent time in the youth academies of Arsenal and Manchester United before joining Hearts, and a return to English football could now be on the cards.

#1266. Omar Marmoush is Quickly Becoming the Next Tanguy Ndombele at Tottenham

Luca Williams-Barnett is the talk of Tottenham Hotspur following his stunning first competitive start against Ipswich Town over the weekend.

The 18-year-old was handed his full debut by Roberto De Zerbi at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and he took full advantage by scoring after 15 minutes, before playing a big part in the second goal scored by Dominic Solanke in the second half.

The teenager is clearly a huge talent, and he showed up some of his more senior teammates with his stunning display against the Tractor Boys, which will leave some fearing for their spots in De Zerbi's XI and squad.

Competition for places in the frontline is already fierce and that's even with Savio, Mykhailo Mudryk, Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons currently out of action through injury, and Richarlison cast aside after failing to secure a summer move away from north London.

James Maddison, Dominic Solanke and Mohammed Kudus were the other players named in the front four alongside Williams-Barnett on Saturday, which left the likes of Dejan Kulusevski and Omar Marmoush on the substitutes' bench.

Marmoush hasn't quite made the impact some were hoping for when he signed for Tottenham in August.

The 27-year-old joined Spurs from Manchester City on loan with an obligation to make the deal permanent for £60million next summer, as Roberto De Zerbi strengthened his attacking department.

But it's fair to suggest that Marmoush hasn't hit the ground running in north London. Indeed, the Egyptian has scored just once in 11 appearances for Spurs, and that came in the 3-1 win against Coventry City last month.

Marmoush has had his fair share of game time as well. Before Saturday's visit of Ipswich Town, he had started in eight of Tottenham's previous nine matches, becoming a regular member in De Zerbi's starting line-up.

But he was dropped down to the bench for the game against Ipswich with Dominic Solanke replacing him up front. Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was another to start, as he came in for the injured Mathys Tel.

Although Spurs do still look a little toothless at times, Solanke and Williams-Barnett both scored in a 2-0 win against Ipswich, proving De Zerbi's decision to be the right one, and they both deserve to keep their place for the trip to Sunderland.

Where does this leave Marmoush? Right now, he is going to have to fight for his place in De Zerbi's first-choice XI. With Tottenham boasting a strong squad and expected to dip into the market for a new No.9 in January, he has no other choice.

But with Marmoush struggling and not having the desired impact some Tottenham fans wanted, there are fears he could turn out to be the next Tanguy Ndombele, who joined Spurs for a big fee and with such huge hopes but didn't perform at the required level.

Ndombele arrived at Tottenham for £63m from Lyon in 2019, a then club-record deal. However, the Frenchman flattered to deceive. Prior to his move to Spurs, he was considered as one of the most exciting up-and-coming midfielders in Europe.

He had this impressive swagger about him and his technical attributes were eye-catching, but he did not deliver on a regular basis and flopped in north London, leaving the club in 2024 to sign for Nice on a permanent deal.

Yes, it's early days, but Marmoush could end up like Ndombele if he doesn't improve, given the huge money spent on the ex-Eintracht Frankfurt forward and the expectations Tottenham fans had when he was signed.

Marmoush has often been used in the centre forward role by De Zerbi this season, but he may have to use him elsewhere to get the best out of them. That includes shifting him back into the No.10 position when James Maddison is rotated. He can also be used on the left, but with Williams-Barnett, Savinho, Tel and Mykhalio Mudryk all competing for that spot, he is needed centrally.

Tottenham need more from Marmoush, and fast, starting with the trip to Sunderland this weekend.

Tottenham made it four wins from five with a comfortable 2-0 success against Ipswich on Saturday, and there were a number of players that stood out

#1265. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

Joao Felix is attracting interest from five European clubs, with Chelsea and Tottenham among the sides considering a move for the Al-Nassr forward ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

The Portuguese international has been playing in Saudi Arabia since leaving European football in the summer of 2025, but a return to the continent could be on the cards amid growing interest in his services.

According to an exclusive report from 4-4-2, Napoli are currently showing the strongest interest in signing the 26-year-old. The Italian outfit are keen to strengthen their attacking options with a creative player who can contribute goals, and Félix is seen as a fit.

#1263. Forget De Ligt: Pochettino Knows He Must Sell Man Utd Star Lisandro Martinez

Mauricio Pochettino will be under no illusions as to the task ahead of him after Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool in his first match in charge.

The Argentine head coach knew that a point would be enough to take Man United out of the Premier League relegation zone following a disastrous start to the season, but those hopes almost ended after just eight minutes when Leny Yoro was given a straight red card after bringing Alexander Isak down just outside the penalty area as he bore down on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick and the hosts never looked back, with further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz wrapping up a comfortable win for Andoni Iraola's men.

Pochettino would have known the Red Devils' shortcomings coming into the clash against Liverpool, and there is plenty to fix as he looks to revolutionise United, but their defensive issues in particular were highlighted again at Anfield.

There were big question marks over the involvement of Matthijs de Ligt in the opening goal, as he failed to challenge for the ball that led to Isak being left one-on-one with Yoro.

The Dutchman had been handed his first Premier League minutes for almost one year following injury, and he was miles off the pace as Iraola's attackers took full advantage.

The 27-year-old still has two-and-a-half years remaining on his contract at Old Trafford but, based on his latest showing, it would be no surprise to see United cash in on the former Juventus star in 2027.

If truth be told, club chiefs need to carry out major surgery on the whole backline, with extra depth and upgrades needed in every one of the defensive positions.

Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot can be effective full-backs when they are fit and available, but United need better competition for them, while Shaw could be on his way out next summer anyway when his contract expires.

The Red Devils have big problems at the heart of their defence though, and Lisandro Martinez needs to be sold in January.

It appears likely that Martinez will be on his way out of Old Trafford in the summer anyway when his contract expires, but United should bring his exit forward by six months.

The Red Devils have the option to extend the Argentina international's contract by a further 12 months, having signed him for a fee of £57m in 2022, but reports suggest that they may not even do that as they look to offload him in 2027.

There was hope that the centre-back, nicknamed 'the Butcher', would be a top signing for United and the early signs were promising.

Lisandro Martinez Injury Record at United

However, the South American defender has ultimately been another failed signing for United, especially in more recent times, while he has also suffered from his fair share of injury problems.

The 28-year-old has become an increasing liability at the back, with United now having the worst defensive record of any team in the top five European leagues this term.

Following the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid last month, Martinez publicly called out Jason Wilcox for the club's recruitment, all while suggesting that some of his teammates aren't at the required level.

That surely won't have gone down well in the dressing room, and it's difficult to see how a player comes back from direct criticism of a director of football.

Wilcox is said to have given the Argentine a 'dressing down' as he was fined and made a public apology, but he isn't showing the quality to prove that he has a future at the Theatre of Dreams beyond this season.

An exit for Martinez next summer seems inevitable, but United should be getting rid of him even sooner than that as they look to begin a defensive rebuild.

#1262. Daily briefing: Can you spot the ‘tortured phrases’?

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Hello Nature readers, would you like to get this Briefing in your inbox free every day? Sign up here.

Today, as of 10:16 GMT, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has journeyed one light-day, or 25.9 billion kilometres, from Earth — farther than any human-made object has gone before. At this distance, signals from Earth’s surface travelling at light speed will take a full 24 hours to reach the craft. The trailblazing probe is expected to lose communications with Earth in 2029, when its plutonium power finally dies. But that time might not signal the end of Voyager 1’s contributions — the craft carries a golden record engraved with sights and sounds from Earth, an interspecies message for any aliens who might encounter it as it continues its journey.

A device that stimulates the brain with flickering light and rhythmic clicking sounds has failed to slow memory loss in people with Alzheimer’s disease. The Spectris AD headset is designed to induce brain activity called gamma waves, which have been linked to increased attention and memory. The results of a long-anticipated clinical trial showed that participants who used the device did not show robust improvements in their cognitive function after a year of treatment compared with those assigned to a sham treatment. The results were reported at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease meeting on 16 November.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status amid an outbreak that’s caused more than 5,700 infections and 10 deaths this year. The US had eliminated measles in 2000 after an intensive vaccination campaign. But declining vaccination rates in the past few years have left pockets of the population vulnerable to infection. “We’ve taken an enormous step back in public health,” says virologist Paul Offit. Measles has also been re-established in Mexico and Bolivia, PAHO announced.

Source: International Vaccine Access Center, Johns Hopkins University

Consumer tests that promise to reveal the full range of microbes living in your gut are taking off — but their results can vary widely. “This is an industry that’s running wild,” says genomicist Jacques Ravel, who co-authored a study that tested several providers. With regard to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”. But it’s hard to set those standards, writes journalist Amber Dance, who sent off her own stool to investigate the field. Part of the problem is that “there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample”, she says.

The proportion of reviewers at Nature who are early-career researchers. Increasing it would benefit all researchers and science as a whole, argues a Nature editorial. (Nature | 6 min read)

Amid the tedium of investigating potentially fraudulent papers, “there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers”, writes research-integrity sleuth Dorothy Bishop. Bishop and Nature’s careers team have compiled a quiz to test your ability to match ‘tortured phrases’ — those that replace common words with synonyms in an attempt to skirt past plagiarism-detection software — with their original text.

From the Bering Strait to Doggerland, much of human history occurred in places that are now underwater, covered by the sea-level rise that occurs after ice ages. Geographer Jerome Dobson has dubbed this drowned land ‘Aquaterra’. It’s the site of many discoveries — such as Blinkerwall in the Baltic Sea, one of Europe’s oldest and largest Stone Age structures — and possibly many more to come. It also offers an interesting thought experiment: if we continue to drive global warming, what might future archaeologists make of our inundated world?

The Atlantic | 29 min read, intermittent paywall

Reference: Geographical Review paper (from 2014)

California congressman Jared Huffman is among the US delegates at the COP31 climate conference in Turkey. He says that the success of a climate-friendly party in recent elections will revive the country’s participation in global negotiations. (The Guardian | 6 min read)

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03791-9

#1261. Edvin Austbo is Quickly Becoming Another West Ham Flop Like Taty Castellanos

West Ham United's frustrating season continued as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Preston North End at the London Stadium on Saturday.

Having won just six of their opening 15 league matches this term prior to the clash against the Lilywhites, West Ham and new manager Scott Parker knew that even three points wouldn't be enough to take them into the playoff positions.

However, even though they were playing the bottom club at home, they had to settle for a point despite dominating proceedings, leaving them in 10th position and three points adrift of the top eight.

The Irons face two in-form teams in Portsmouth and Stoke City next, as Parker looks to pick up his first win since replacing Nuno Espirito Santo in the dugout, having so far taken two points from nine available.

There is no doubt that West Ham have the squad to run away with the Championship title, but it simply hasn't happened for them yet.

The east London outfit can't be criticised too much for their final third exploits given they have scored 38 goals in their 16 Championship fixtures this term, but their record of 24 goals conceded is more than anyone else in the top 10, and higher than Portsmouth and Wrexham below them.

Teams West Ham Have Conceded First to This Season

West Ham are continuously giving themselves a lot to do to win games by conceding the first goal, and it is a habit they need to break if they are to move back up to the table.

Despite having experienced players like Konstantinos Mavropanos, Max Kilman and Kyle Walker-Peters at the back, the Irons are struggling from a defensive point of view, and it is seeing fans turn on them.

While West Ham have been largely prolific going the other way, there have been some disappointing players in attack too.

While Jarrod Bowen continues to be a talisman for West Ham in England's second tier, the same cannot be said for others like Taty Castellanos and Edvin Austbo.

West Ham raised eyebrows when they paid more than £25m to sign the former in the January transfer window, with the Argentine saying he would give everything in a claret and blue shirt.

While the 28-year-old was unable to keep the Irons in the Premier League, despite scoring six goals in 18 appearances, he did impress the London Stadium faithful.

Having remained at the club over the summer, the expectation was that he'd be a big hit in the Championship, but instead he has become a big transfer flop.

Castellanos has one goal in 15 league appearances, with that coming in the 6-0 thrashing of Wrexham back in September.

The South American striker reportedly wants to leave the club, which suggests he feels he is too good for the Championship, even though he is currently stinking the place out, and fans are beginning to turn on him.

Expectations were also high that summer signing Austbo could prove to be an exciting addition in the second tier this term.

West Ham agreed a fee of around €13m, which is a big fee for the second tier, to sign the 21-year-old, who helped Viking FK win their first Norwegian league title in 34 years in 2025.

Austbo is known for his pace and intelligence on the pitch, but his impact has been lacking so far in the claret and blue.

He has two goals and two assists for the Irons so far this term, but you would probably expect his goal contribution numbers to be higher in a team which has scored 38 league goals.

Austbo has started Parker's previous two matches in charge, having come off the bench in his first game against Cardiff, but he has been taken off before the hour-mark in both.

The Norwegian attacker was guilty of losing the ball in a key area which led to Preston's opener on Saturday and, after failing to create a single chance, was handed a 3/10 rating for his display.

As things stand, Austbo is quickly becoming a big-money transfer flop, and he needs to improve quickly to start repaying his fee.
